context.title: Amnon, Tamar and Absalom
context.summary: David's eldest son Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar and then throws her out. David is furious but does nothing. Two years later Tamar's brother Absalom has Amnon killed at a sheep-shearing feast and flees to his grandfather, the king of Geshur.
context.background: Amnon was David's firstborn and heir; Tamar was Absalom's full sister. The law forbade relations between half-siblings (Leviticus 18:9). Tamar's words 'do not thou this folly' (v. 12) echo the outrage at Shechem in Genesis 34:7. Nathan's warning that the sword would not depart from David's house (12:10) begins to unfold.

customs.note: A long, richly made robe worn by the king's unmarried daughters. Tearing it and putting ashes on her head were signs of grief and ruin.

watchFor: Tamar pleads for her honor and Amnon's (vv. 12–13).
'He was very wroth' (v. 21), but David does not act.
Absalom says nothing to Amnon for two full years (vv. 22–23).

w: and let her cause to eat me

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Absalom
people.summary: Father of peace; i.e., “peaceful” David’s son by Maacah (2 Sam. 3:3; comp. 1 Kings 1:6). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head (2 Sam. 14:25,26).

people.name: Amnon
people.summary: The eldest son of David, by Ahinoam of Jezreel (1 Chr. 3:1; 2 Sam. 3:2).

people.name: Tamar
people.summary: A daughter of David (2 Sam. 13:1-32; 1 Chr. 3:9), whom Amnon shamefully outraged and afterwards “hated exceedingly,” thereby illustrating the law of human nature noticed even by the heathen, “Proprium humani ingenii est odisse quem laeseris”, i.e., “It is the property of human nature to hate one whom you have injured.”

people.name: Jonadab
people.summary: Son of Shammah, and David’s nephew, and also one of his chief warriors (2 Sam. 21:21).

people.name: Shammah
people.summary: One of the sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:9).

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Talmai
people.summary: A king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after he had put Amnon to death (2 Sam. 3:3; 13:37).

people.name: Ammihud
people.summary: The father of Talmai, king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after the murder of Amnon (2 Sam. 13:37).

places.name: Baal-hazor
places.summary: Having a courtyard, or Baal’s village, the place on the borders of Ephraim and Benjamin where Absalom held the feast of sheep-shearing when Amnon was assassinated (2 Sam. 13:23).

places.name: Geshur
places.summary: Bridge, the name of a district or principality of Syria near Gilead, between Mount Hermon and the Lake of Tiberias (2 Sam. 15:8; 1 Chr. 2:23).

events.title: Reign of David
events.summary: Passage: 2 Samuel 2:1–24:25. People: David. Place: Hebron, Jerusalem. Lasted about 40 years.
